title: Page-table walkthrough
objectives: Translate several addresses using one page table
Recognise an address whose page has no frame

blocks.text: Use this page table with a 4 KiB page size. Page 0 maps to frame 7, page 1 to frame 2, page 2 to frame 9, and page 3 to frame 5. Page 4 has no frame.
Virtual address 3,000 is below 4,096, so it is page 0 with offset 3,000. Frame 7 starts at 7 × 4,096 = 28,672, so the physical address is 28,672 + 3,000 = 31,672.
Virtual address 5,000 = 1 × 4,096 + 904, so it is page 1 with offset 904. Frame 2 starts at 8,192, so the physical address is 8,192 + 904 = 9,096.
Virtual address 9,000 = 2 × 4,096 + 808, so it is page 2 with offset 808. Frame 9 starts at 36,864, so the physical address is 36,864 + 808 = 37,672.
When the page has no frame

Virtual address 17,000 = 4 × 4,096 + 616, so it falls in page 4. The table has no frame for page 4, so the hardware cannot finish the translation and raises a page fault. The operating system then decides whether the access is valid and, if so, brings the page into memory.

blocks.title: A check you can always do
blocks.text: The physical address and the virtual address must have the same offset. If your two offsets differ, you made an arithmetic error.

blocks.question: Using the page table above (4 KiB pages), what is the physical address for virtual address 9,000?
blocks.explanation: 9,000 = 2 × 4,096 + 808, so it is page 2 with offset 808. Page 2 maps to frame 9, which starts at 36,864. Adding the offset gives 37,672.
